gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the battery ratings of the picks on one basis. Logitech's US pages give the G435 18 h and the G321 '20+ hours' with no stated volume, mode or test condition. SoundGuys (a cited result) measured the G435 at over 24 h in its own testing. Budget-brand figures such as EKSA's are rated with the lights off and fall sharply with them on.
standout_why: I compared against SoundGuys' budget list (cited) and gamecuki's wireless under-$50 list (a top result, not cited). I also opened RTINGS' wireless and under-$50 lists and PC Gamer's wireless list, but those fetches returned only navigation or a title, and Vaagame failed on a certificate error, so I couldn't read their figures. SoundGuys already gives its own G435 result ('over 24 hours in testing'). Gamecuki already gives lights-on vs lights-off hours (EKSA E900WT: 80 h vs 30 h) and per-mode hours (Acer: 80 h on 2.4 GHz vs 100 h on Bluetooth). Gamecuki gives HyperX Cloud Jet as 'up to 25 hours' with no mode or condition. None of them puts the picks side by side on one basis. The finding that would decide the pick is whether the Cloud Jet's 25 h is the Bluetooth figure and its 2.4 GHz figure is lower. I could not source it: HyperX and HP returned 429 or timed out, and a datasheet I had saved could not be read.
decides: This confirms rather than changes the pick, and it should change two lines on the page. (1) The G321 is $54.99 on Logitech's US store today ($59.99 list), so it is over the $50 budget, not the '~$49–50' ChatGPT gave. (2) Battery hours in the table need a footnote naming the basis of each figure: maker claim with no condition (Logitech), lights off (EKSA), or a reviewer's measurement (SoundGuys on the G435). Otherwise the EKSA rows' 36–60 h look 2–3× better than the G435's 18 h on a basis the makers never stated. If the HyperX 2.4 GHz figure can be sourced (snippets point to about 20 h in dongle mode vs 25 h on Bluetooth, at 50% volume), the Cloud Jet's 25 h headline should be cut to its dongle figure for gaming use.
